# Tabs

Header: `winui/ui/navigation/Tabs.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/navigation/Tabs.hpp`.

A strip of tabs over the selected tab's content.

The view owns every tab's content but only measures, arranges and renders the selected tab's content. Each tab has a key ([Tab::key](#uitab-key), else its header) that the events report and that stays with it when it is dragged elsewhere. The close button, a middle click and Ctrl+F4 remove the tab and select its neighbor. With an [on_tab_close_requested()](#on_tab_close_requested) handler they raise that instead, and the handler decides, calling [remove_tab()](#remove_tab) to close it. The "+" button shows once there is an [on_add_tab_button_click()](#on_add_tab_button_click) handler, unless [set_add_tab_button_visible()](#set_add_tab_button_visible) says otherwise. [Tabs](#uitabs) that do not fit scroll, and dragging a tab reorders the strip. The declarative form is [ui::Tabs](#uitabs).

Example: 
```cpp
auto  owned = std::make_unique<ui::TabsControl>();
auto* tabs  = owned.get();
tabs->add_tab("Home", std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Start here"));
tabs->add_tab(ui::Tab{ .header  = "Document 1",
                       .key     = "doc-1",
                       .icon    = ui::IconGlyph{0xE8A5},
                       .content = std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Hello") });
tabs->set_closable(0, false);
tabs->on_add_tab_button_click([tabs] {
    tabs->add_tab("New document", std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Empty"));
    tabs->set_selected_index(tabs->tab_count() - 1);
});
tabs->on_selection_changed([](const std::string& key) { std::println("tab {}", key); });
window.set_content(std::move(owned));
```

## `ui::Tabs`

A tab strip over swappable content. Builds a [ui::TabsControl](#uitabscontrol). The first tab is selected unless [`.selected_key`](#uitabs-selected_key) names another. A tab's close button removes it, unless [`.on_tab_close_requested`](#uitabs-on_tab_close_requested) is set. Then the handler decides, and closes the tab by calling remove_tab() through [`.control`](#uitabs-control). The "+" shows once [`.on_add_tab_button_click`](#uitabs-on_add_tab_button_click) is set.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::Tabs>     tabs;
ui::Property<std::string> current;
int                       documents = 1;

window.set_content(ui::Tabs{
    .selected_key            = current, // "home", then whichever tab the user picks
    .tab_width_mode          = ui::TabsWidthMode::SizeToContent,
    .on_tab_close_requested  = [&](const std::string& key) { tabs->remove_tab(key); },
    .on_add_tab_button_click = [&] {
        tabs->add_tab(ui::Tab{.header = "New document", .key = std::format("doc-{}", ++documents)});
        tabs->set_selected_index(tabs->tab_count() - 1);
    },
    .control = tabs,
    .items   = {
        ui::Tab{ .header = "Home", .key = "home", .closable = false, .content = ui::Text{ .text = "Start here" } },
        ui::Tab{ .header = "Document 1", .key = "doc-1", .content = ui::Text{ .text = "Hello" } },
    },
});
```

```cpp
    .selected_key, .tab_width_mode, .close_button_overlay_mode, .add_tab_button_visible,
    .can_reorder_tabs, .strip_background, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width,

}
```

## `ui::Tab`

One tab: a header, an optional icon, and the content shown while it is selected. Written inside the `.items` of a [ui::Tabs](#uitabs), or handed to [TabsControl::add_tab()](#add_tab). The content is a spec or an already built [`std::unique_ptr<Element>`](../tree/element.md).

Example: 
```cpp
auto tabs = std::make_unique<ui::TabsControl>();
tabs->add_tab(ui::Tab{ .header = "Document 1", .key = "doc-1", .icon = ui::IconGlyph{0xE8A5},
                       .content = ui::Text{ .text = "Hello" } });
tabs->add_tab(ui::Tab{
    .header   = "Settings",
    .key      = "settings",
    .icon     = ui::IconGlyph{0xE713},
    .closable = false,
    .content  = std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Settings go here"),
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Tab{
    .header, .key, .icon, .closable, .content
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uitab-header"></span>`header` | `ui::Binding<std::string>` |  | The tab's caption, and its tooltip. A bound header follows its property. A tab without [`.key`](#uitab-key) keeps the key made from its first header. |
| <span id="uitab-key"></span>`key` | `std::string` |  | What identifies the tab in `.selected_key` and the close and selection events. Empty takes the header, numbered " (2)", " (3)", ... after the first tab with it. It stays with the tab when the tab is dragged elsewhere or renamed. |
| <span id="uitab-icon"></span>`icon` | `ui::IconSource` |  | The icon before the header in its 16-DIP box: a [Symbol](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#symbol), a glyph or a path in the header's color, or a picture in its own colors. Empty shows none. |
| <span id="uitab-closable"></span>`closable` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the close button and accepts middle click and Ctrl+F4. |
| <span id="uitab-content"></span>`content` | `ui::Spec` |  | What the [Tabs](#uitabs) shows while this tab is selected; owned by the [Tabs](#uitabs) once added. |

## `ui::TabList`

A built, owned list of tabs. A braced list of [`ui::Tab{...}`](#uitab) converts to it, building each tab's content as it goes.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::TabList tabs = { ui::Tab{ .header = "One", .content = ui::Text{ .text = "1" } },
                     ui::Tab{ .header = "Two", .content = ui::Text{ .text = "2" } } };
window.set_content(ui::Tabs{ .items = std::move(tabs) });
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::TabList{
    .entries
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uitablist-entries"></span>`entries` | `std::vector<Entry>` |  | The tabs, in strip order. |

## `ui::TabsControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ValueProvider`, `ui::SelectionProvider`.

A strip of tabs over the selected tab's content.

The view owns every tab's content but only measures, arranges and renders the selected tab's content. Each tab has a key ([Tab::key](#uitab-key), else its header) that the events report and that stays with it when it is dragged elsewhere. The close button, a middle click and Ctrl+F4 remove the tab and select its neighbor. With an [on_tab_close_requested()](#on_tab_close_requested) handler they raise that instead, and the handler decides, calling [remove_tab()](#remove_tab) to close it. The "+" button shows once there is an [on_add_tab_button_click()](#on_add_tab_button_click) handler, unless [set_add_tab_button_visible()](#set_add_tab_button_visible) says otherwise. [Tabs](#uitabs) that do not fit scroll, and dragging a tab reorders the strip. The declarative form is [ui::Tabs](#uitabs).

Example: 
```cpp
auto  owned = std::make_unique<ui::TabsControl>();
auto* tabs  = owned.get();
tabs->add_tab("Home", std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Start here"));
tabs->add_tab(ui::Tab{ .header  = "Document 1",
                       .key     = "doc-1",
                       .icon    = ui::IconGlyph{0xE8A5},

    tabs->add_tab("New document", std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Empty"));
```

```cpp

```

A turn over an overflowing strip scrolls the strip. Otherwise the turn reaches the tab's content through [handle_wheel()](../tree/element.md#handle_wheel), so a scrollable inside the tab wins over one wrapping the whole [Tabs](#uitabs).

### hit_test_children

```cpp
void hit_test_children(Point p, std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

The children `p` (in this element's layout coordinates) is tested against, topmost first. Default: what [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists, last first. A container that draws in another order ([Panel](../layout/panel.md#uipanel)'s z-index), a control with parts [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) does not list, or one whose parts cover others in places (a pane drawn over the content) lists them here.

The ring's corner radius: the theme's control radius by default.

### focus_ring_inside

```cpp
bool focus_ring_inside() const override
```

Whether the ring goes inside [focus_ring_rect()](#focus_ring_rect) in every era, its outer edge on the rect. False by default, which leaves it to the theme. An item inside a viewport (a list row, a tab, a menu item) returns true, as does a control in a tight spot, so a neighbor or the viewport edge never cuts its ring.

## Enumerations

### TabsWidthMode

```cpp
enum class TabsWidthMode
```

How a [Tabs](#uitabs) control sizes its tabs.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Equal` | The strip divided evenly, each tab clamped to 100..240 DIPs (the default). |
| `SizeToContent` | Each tab as wide as its icon, header and close button. |
| `Compact` | Unselected tabs shrink to their icon. |

### TabsCloseButtonOverlayMode

```cpp
enum class TabsCloseButtonOverlayMode
```

When a closable tab shows its close button.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Auto` | the same as Always |
| `OnPointerOver` | on the selected tab and the hovered one |
| `Always` | on every closable tab |
